lesson.guided.prompt: Your turn! Let's find the answer.
lesson.ready: Great work! You're ready to practise.
lesson.ADD-01.hook: Fanak has some dates. A friend brings more. How many now?
lesson.ADD-01.model: Tap the blue dates to put them with the others.
lesson.ADD-02.hook: A ten-frame has 10 spaces. It helps us count fast!
lesson.ADD-02.model: We have 6. Tap 3 more spaces to add 3.
lesson.ADD-02.keyIdea: Start at the bigger number and count on.
lesson.ADD-03.hook: Some numbers are friends: together they make 10!
lesson.ADD-03.model: We have 7. Fill the frame. How many did we add?
lesson.ADD-03.keyIdea: 7 and 3 make 10. They are ten friends!
lesson.ADD-04.hook: Fanak hops on a number line. Let's add bigger numbers!
lesson.ADD-04.keyIdea: Make 10 first: 8 and 2 make 10, then 3 more is 13.
lesson.ADD-05.hook: Big numbers have tens and ones.
lesson.ADD-05.model: Put the blocks together. Count the tens, then the ones.
lesson.ADD-05.keyIdea: Add ones to ones and tens to tens.
lesson.ADD-06.hook: Sometimes the ones make more than 10!
lesson.ADD-06.model: Put the blocks together, then trade 10 ones for a ten.
lesson.ADD-06.keyIdea: 10 ones make 1 ten. We call this regrouping.
lesson.ADD-07.hook: Now we add hundreds, tens and ones.
lesson.ADD-07.model: Put the blocks together and trade when you have 10.
lesson.ADD-07.keyIdea: Add each column, starting with the ones.
lesson.SUB-01.hook: Fanak has 5 dates and eats some. How many are left?
lesson.SUB-02.hook: Let's take away using a ten-frame.
lesson.SUB-02.model: We have 9. Tap 4 counters to take them away.
lesson.SUB-02.keyIdea: Start at the bigger number and count back.
lesson.SUB-03.hook: A whole is made of two parts. Can we find a missing part?
lesson.SUB-03.model: We have 4. Bring 3 more. That makes 7.
lesson.SUB-03.keyIdea: 4 and 3 make 7, so 7 take away 4 is 3.
lesson.SUB-04.hook: Let's hop back on the number line!
lesson.SUB-04.keyIdea: Go back to 10 first: 13 take away 3 is 10, then 2 more is 8.
lesson.SUB-05.hook: We can take away tens and ones.
lesson.SUB-05.keyIdea: Take ones from ones and tens from tens.
lesson.SUB-06.hook: What if there aren't enough ones?
lesson.SUB-06.model: Trade 1 ten for 10 ones, then take away 17.
lesson.SUB-06.keyIdea: Trading a ten for 10 ones is called regrouping.
lesson.SUB-07.model: Trade so each column has enough, then take away.
lesson.SUB-07.keyIdea: Start with the ones. Borrow from the next column when needed.
lesson.MUL-01.hook: Fanak puts dates on plates in equal groups.
lesson.MUL-02.hook: Rows of palm trees make an array.
lesson.MUL-02.model: Build 3 rows of 4. Then turn it around!
lesson.MUL-03.hook: Some times facts are extra easy!
lesson.MUL-03.keyIdea: × 0 makes 0, × 1 stays the same, × 10 adds a zero.
lesson.MUL-04.hook: Times 4 is double and double again.
lesson.MUL-05.hook: We can use facts we know!
lesson.DIV-01.hook: Fanak shares dates fairly with friends.
lesson.DIV-01.model: Share 12 dates on 3 plates. Give one to each plate at a time.
lesson.DIV-01.keyIdea: 12 shared into 3 is 4 each. We write 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
lesson.DIV-02.hook: We can also make groups of the same size.
lesson.DIV-04.hook: Let's use times 3 and times 4 facts to divide.
lesson.DIV-05.hook: Times 6 and 7 facts help us divide.

manip.numberLine.label: Number line. Use the arrow keys to hop.

manip.plates.summaryDone: {a} dates shared on {b} plates: {each} on each plate.
